subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw add Discord channel/account-level granular message gates for send/read/edit/delete, or should the existing generic `tools.message.actions.allow` policy remain the supported control for removing destructive message actions?
rationale: Both paths are technically viable, but the choice changes public config shape, per-account inheritance, generated metadata, and least-privilege semantics for destructive Discord message actions.

options.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
options.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions` contract that distinguishes send/read/edit/delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

options.title: Document Generic Allowlist Only
options.body: Treat `tools.message.actions.allow` and per-agent allowlists as the supported way to remove destructive actions, avoiding another Discord-specific config surface.

options.title: Defer For Cross-Channel Design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers choose a broader cross-channel action-gate model instead of adding a Discord-specific shape now.

recommendation.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
recommendation.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions` contract that distinguishes send/read/edit/delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord messaging runtime/config ownership plus prior review context make this the best available owner for the config/security contract choice.
